coordinates: UTF-16, zero-based, half-open, relative to unescaped SQL without a dialect header
representationNotes: SQL is after host bind/slot replacement. :min_id is a bind. src() is a relation slot only when unqualified, zero-argument and matching the case-sensitive relations key. Bare src is a physical identifier, not shorthand for a slot.

relations and physicalTables map names to fact-set ids. Caret column tuples are [columnId, visibleRelation, optionalOutputName, optionalNullability, optionalOrigin, optionalNavigationId]. Null or missing overrides retain facts. Empty visibleRelation is an unqualified projected or computed row. completionColumns overrides the displayed prefix-filtered inventory, not the scope inventory.

Reference targets are compact ids for passthrough columns, computed.<name> for computed outputs and physical.<name> for physical columns. Resolve an id against the declared caret column tuples with the same output name as the reference text, yielding an explicit (visibleRelation, column, navigationId) target. Empty targets means unresolved, including ambiguous names. navigationTargets can separately enumerate an ambiguity chooser's declarations. Ranges cover the column identifier, not its qualifier. Navigation ids are opaque; harnesses materialize their own real declaration locations.

Trino and Doris must consume identical post-replacement SQL. Their current Brikk replacements also use src(). A bare-slot adapter must record an offset mapping rather than reinterpret physical bare src. Native table-type hooks and AST walkers are separate result axes.

Native resolve results can retain the original declaration's alias behind a CTE or subquery. Compare the exposed relation from the syntactic qualifier or native immediateQualifier, while retaining the independent declaration navigationId; do not mistake an origin alias for a leaked visible alias.

Authored engine SQL is independent of the implementation under test. A witness probes the input row at the caret or the relevant transform, not necessarily remaining row filters. For example, joined nullable inputs are witnessed before WHERE; LIMIT and sampling witnesses prove schema, not row selection. SQL type and Kotlin display type are independent. UNKNOWN is unavailable, not FULL with no columns. Partial-contract warnings describe guarantees, not native binder failures.
The pinned DuckDB engine has no RIGHT SEMI/ANTI syntax. Their witnesses swap inputs and use SEMI/ANTI, proving the same preserved-side semantics without relying on a core lowering implementation.

COMPUTED includes stage/clause results and set outputs without unique passthrough lineage. Renaming one proven column retains Kotlin type and navigation. Arithmetic and aggregates do not inherit Kotlin operand declarations.

evidence.aliases: DuckDB aliases replace source names; explicit derived projections expose output names, not inner qualifiers. https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/query_syntax/from
evidence.ctes: CTEs expose projected rows; inner WITH bindings shadow outer bindings. https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/query_syntax/with
evidence.subqueries: Derived projections and correlated range-variable lookup; local aliases hide outer aliases. https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/expressions/subqueries
evidence.joins: Outer joins make unmatched sides nullable. SEMI/ANTI expose the preserved side; RIGHT variants preserve the right side. https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/query_syntax/from#joins
evidence.diagnostics: FULL proves absence; PARTIAL does not. The native binder rejects missing/ambiguous references. Contract guarantees and runtime schema are separate facts.
evidence.navigation: Provider navigation, including relation-fallback targets, is supplied, never inferred from SQL types.
evidence.coordinates: JVM UTF-16 indexing: the emoji occupies two code units. Named binds have already been replaced.
evidence.clauses: DuckDB exposes SELECT aliases in GROUP BY and ORDER BY. https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/dialect/friendly_sql#query-features
evidence.set-operations: Set operations use left output names but have no unique Kotlin origin across two sources. https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/query_syntax/setops
evidence.slot-identity: Provider keys identify Kotlin parameters, not SQL case-folded function names. Argument-bearing/qualified calls are not slots; bare names are physical identifiers.
evidence.pipe-preserving: WHERE, ORDER BY, LIMIT, OFFSET, DISTINCT and TABLESAMPLE preserve schema. https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/pipe-syntax
evidence.lineage: SELECT/RENAME passthrough preserves single-column lineage; explicit projections hide input qualifiers. https://cloud.google.com/bigquery/docs/reference/standard-sql/pipe-syntax
evidence.computed: EXTEND/WINDOW add results; AGGREGATE retains group keys and named aggregates. COUNT, ROW_NUMBER, literal 1 and integer multiplication of non-null inputs are non-null, without Kotlin operand lineage.
evidence.knowledge: Unknown/partial stars cannot close an empty row. CALL without an output contract cannot promise input columns. Computed additions remain enumerable with unknown input.
evidence.pipe-changing: SET replaces, DROP removes, RENAME preserves lineage, PIVOT/UNPIVOT transform schemas. Independent native oracle queries exercise their ordinary relational equivalents.
evidence.stars: Stars include joined rows and nullable sides; qualified stars select only that range variable. https://duckdb.org/docs/stable/sql/expressions/star
evidence.physical: DAS table columns are relation facts too; ordinary SQL and PIPE must expose them without inventing Kotlin types.
evidence.incomplete: Caret completion offers provable input columns before missing syntax. The current identifier ev is syntactically valid but absent from a FULL contract, so its missing-column diagnostic remains correct even while completion offers event_kind; an unfinished parenthesis is missing syntax, not a missing column.
evidence.positions: Relation names and string literals are not column-expression completion positions.
